topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets out the scope of the cancer lecture series, and outlines the key learning objectives.

topics.label: Intrinsic and environmental drivers of cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental nature of cancer and explore the interplay between endogenous mutational processes, environmental exposures, and epidemiological evidence in determining cancer risk.

topics.label: Infectious agents and cancer pathogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how various pathogens drive oncogenesis, with a detailed focus on the co-factors and molecular events underlying Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical and physical mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how specific environmental, dietary, and chemical carcinogens, alongside UV radiation, undergo metabolic activation to induce DNA damage and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, inflammation, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic drivers of cancer, distinguishing initiation from promotional processes driven by inflammation, signaling activation, and developmental susceptibility.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and evaluating carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic signatures, epidemiological biobanks, in vivo models, and in vitro assays used to identify and test carcinogenic agents.

topics.label: Conclusion and risk-benefit considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the lecture's closing framing, summarising environmental carcinogenicity in the context of everyday risk-benefit decisions.
